title: Club Agreement

contents.title: Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Reasonableness of Terms.

html:
This Club Agreement (this “Agreement”), dated as of ___________________________ (the “Effective Date”) is by and between ______________________ (the “Club”) located at ______________________________________ and MYDANCR LLC (the “Company”).

WHEREAS, the Club represents that it is duly organized or lawfully operated, has authority to enter this Agreement, maintains all licenses required for its premises and offers, and will comply with the law;

WHEREAS, the Company is a duly organized and lawfully in the business of Internet marketing and promotion;

WHEREAS, the Company wishes to enter into an agreement with the Club for the purposes of promoting and marketing the Club and its dancers to the general public;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises, representations, warranties, covenants, and conditions set forth in this Agreement, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and adequacy of which is hereby acknowledged, the Parties mutually agree as follows:

1. Term and Termination.

Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Company and the Club agree that term of this Agreement shall be effective for a period of twelve (12) months. The Company may suspend or terminate this Agreement at the sole discretion of the Company. The Club remains responsible for accrued fees, valid consumer commitments, and return/destruction of credentials. Public data may be retained as historical/legal records but should not suggest an active relationship after termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement at any time and for any reason with or without cause with thirty days (30) written notice.

2. Compensation.

The Club agrees to pay the Company a monthly fee of _____________ beginning on __________________ and ending on ______________ via a credit card submitted through the Company’s online billing system, unless this Agreement is terminated by either Party. The Company does not have access to the credit card information provided to their credit card processor. All data received and related to the credit card information shall be kept by the processing company.

3. Independent Businesses.

The Club and the Company are independent contractors. The Company does not operate the club, employ or supply dancers, control admission, supervise club workers, sell alcohol, provide security, or guarantee attendance. The Club is solely responsible for premises, licenses, age checks, work cards, employment/classification, wage/tip/fee practices, alcohol, gaming, safety, accessibility, taxes, and house rules. Nothing in this Agreement shall constitute or create a joint venture, partnership, or any other similar arrangement between the Parties. No Party is authorized to act as agent for the other Party hereunder except as expressly stated in this Agreement.

4. Club Requirements.

The Club authorizes the Company to display approved Club name, address, location, hours, directions, website/phone, public media, roster/affiliations, schedules, Club Deals, and other submitted information. The Club shall keep all provided information accurate and has the intellectual property rights to submitted marks and media. The Company may standardize presentation and remove inaccurate or noncompliant content. Public listing and promotion require an approved, active venue page and at least one active approved Club Deal. Loss of eligibility may pause public promotion without erasing private affiliation or required records. Dancer NFC check-in is separate from public listing eligibility. The Club must provide accurate legal, licensing, location, contact, tax, and payment information. Access codes and invitations are single-purpose security credentials and may not be transferred. Authorized owners, managers, and staff may use venue profiles, dashboards, and internal features across devices within their permissions. The Club is responsible for their activity. The Club must train staff, scan customer QR passes, verify applicable offer conditions, maintain connectivity and alternate support steps, honor valid redemptions on published terms, display exclusions clearly, and report compromise. The Club may refuse entry for a lawful disclosed reason but may not falsely mark a redemption or discriminate unlawfully. The Club will maintain all adult-entertainment, cabaret, liquor, fire, occupancy, employment, tax, accessibility, and other licenses and comply with anti-trafficking, age, wage, discrimination, privacy, advertising, and consumer laws. The Club will not use the Company or its services to arrange prostitution, sexual services, unlawful contact, worker coercion, kickbacks, or retaliation. All users of Company’s service must satisfy the Club's lawful age, identification, capacity, dress code, hours, safety, and house rules. A deal may have one redemption per guest, session, time period, or other clearly disclosed limit. Unless the deal says otherwise, it cannot be combined, transferred, resold, or exchanged for cash.

5. Dancer Affiliation Management.

A dancer's affiliation with the Club is established automatically when the Company validates the dancer's intentional tap on the club's official dressing-room NFC tag. No Club representative approval or confirmation is required. An authorized Club user may remove that affiliation through the venue dashboard. Removal affects the club-linked roster, shift eligibility, and Working Now features for that Club; it does not approve or unpublish the dancer's account, profile, identity, age, media, or eligibility for publication and does not transfer the Club's legal verification, licensing, employment, or safety duties to the Company.

The Club must use the venue-dashboard removal control accurately and lawfully. It may remove an affiliation it believes is inaccurate or no longer current, but it may not use removal to retaliate unlawfully, misrepresent employment, obtain private dancer commission, or control unrelated dancer content. The Club should promptly report suspected tag copying, relocation, or misuse to The Company.

5A. Internal Roster and VIP Requests.

The Company's Internal tools let authorized staff manage the Club's roster and table requests. Table links display eligible dancers who chose Internal or Both for the active shift. VIP invitations grant the named recipient access to that Club's private request area; eligible affiliated dancers may be requested for a future date and time even when off shift. The Club must respect dancer visibility choices, limit table links to intended adult patrons, protect staff accounts and invitation links, and promptly revoke compromised links or access. A table link can be used by anyone who obtains it; it is not proof of identity, age, or physical presence.

Table access and admission checks.

Table QR links open the roster immediately without a guest account or acceptance checkbox. A View terms control provides the request notice and policy links; scanning the QR code or viewing the notice is not recorded as affirmative agreement. Anyone using the same table link can see and cancel its open requests. The Club must inform patrons that table requests are shared and remains responsible for legally required age, identity, and admission checks. VIP activation separately records acceptance of the linked User Terms and VIP & Table Access Terms, which does not replace the Club's admission checks or its own visit terms.

The Club must monitor its request inbox, coordinate each dancer's voluntary agreement and availability before confirming, accurately update request status, and communicate applicable admission, pricing, cancellation, and other visit terms to the guest. Staff acknowledgement of a table request means it was seen, not accepted by a dancer. The Company supplies communication tools and does not book, employ, or supply dancers or guarantee availability, attendance, notification delivery, or fulfillment. The Club must not rely solely on alerts or use these features for unlawful services or coercion.

6. NFC Tags.

Dressing-room NFC tags remain Company-controlled property even when installed at the club. The Company has exclusive authority to program, encode, provision, activate, assign, reassign, disable, replace, and reprogram every official dressing-room NFC tag. A validated dancer tap on the official dressing-room tag establishes the dancer's affiliation automatically; it does not require a Club approval step. The Club may install and physically protect an assigned tag only as directed by the Company. The Club may not program, modify, duplicate, redirect, replace, independently activate, or create a lookalike version of any NFC tag or its destination; collect credentials; or bypass the Company's technical validation. The Club must install each tag only at the approved location, restrict staff access, prevent copying or relocation, inspect for tampering, and report loss or compromise immediately.

The Club authorizes collection of the Club time of the event, browser or device information, IP address, the applicable NFC tag, and information reasonably necessary to operate dancer affiliation, time-limited presence, and fraud prevention. The Company does not use geofences or continuous or background location tracking for those functions; the applicable intentional NFC tap is the verification event. The Company may disable or replace a tag for security, misuse, termination, or maintenance.

7. Club Deals.

The Club may publish only approved admission or line-access offers. Each deal must be truthful, available on disclosed terms, and honored when valid, subject only to clearly disclosed capacity, age, dress code, hours, safety, and house rules. The Club may not publish alcohol, drink, bottle-service, sexual-service, cash, gambling, controlled-substance, or unlawful offers. Each offer and its displayed conditions require Company approval before publication; approval of one offer does not approve another.

The Club is the offeror and bears responsibility for consumer disclosures, fulfillment, staff training, and lawful refusal. The Company may review or remove a deal but does not become the offeror.

The Club must honor valid free-entry passes under the displayed conditions and have authorized staff scan customer QR passes to verify the applicable deal; no customer cashier NFC tap is required. Guest-list registration alone does not mean free admission; the Club determines and discloses any cover charge. MyDancr transmits pickup requests and the customer’s name, phone, email, pickup location, and party size to the Club. Once received, the Club alone handles follow-up, arrangements, confirmation, and transportation fulfillment. A submitted request is not a confirmed pickup.

8. Errors, outages, and disputes, If a technical outage the Club may contact Company support at support@mydancr.com with the deal, club, time, and reference so a support ticket can be generated. The Company may review available records, correct a technical error, or deny a claim lacking reliable evidence. Screenshots are not final proof.

Non-Solicitation.

In order to aid in the protection of the Company’s goodwill, confidential information, trade secrets, and other legitimate business interests, the Club hereby further agrees that during the term of this Agreement with the Company and for a period of two years following the termination of this Agreement with the Company (for any reason, either voluntary, involuntary, or mutual agreement) the Club shall not directly or indirectly, for themself or on behalf of any other person or entity, for compensation, or gratuitously:

i. hire, attempt to hire, or assist any other person or entity in hiring or attempting to hire any employee of the Company or;

ii. encourage or assist any person in encouraging any customer, client, or supplier of the Company to terminate or materially reduce its relationship with the Company.

Limitation of Liability.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, exemplary, or punitive damages, or lost profits, revenue, goodwill, data, or business opportunity. Except for accrued payment duties, confidentiality or security breach, indemnity obligations, infringement, fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence, each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement will not exceed the subscription fees paid or payable to the Company under this Agreement during the twelve months before the event giving rise to the claim. A signed written amendment may state a different negotiated cap.

Club Indemnification.

The Club will defend, indemnify, and hold harmless The Company and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, and contractors from and against third-party claims, demands, investigations, proceedings, damages, judgments, settlements, penalties, fines, liabilities, losses, costs, and reasonable attorneys’ fees arising from or relating to:

1. the Club’s premises, operations, security, admission decisions, licenses, permits, regulatory compliance, offers, promotions, fulfillment, submitted content, taxes, or material breach of this Agreement;

1. the acts or omissions of the Club’s owners, officers, employees, contractors, dancers, entertainers, temporary or seasonal employees, staffing-agency personnel, security personnel, vendors, agents, or other persons engaged by or acting for the Club, collectively, “Club Personnel”;

2. the hiring, engagement, compensation, classification, scheduling, supervision, discipline, safety, working conditions, termination, or other employment or contractor practices involving Club Personnel;

3. any allegation by Club Personnel concerning wages, tips, benefits, taxes, worker classification, discrimination, harassment, retaliation, workplace safety, injury, workers’ compensation, or other employment-related rights;

4. any content, representation, offer, instruction, communication, or information submitted or provided by the Club or Club Personnel; or

5. personal injury, death, property damage, unlawful conduct, or violation of another person’s rights occurring at the Club or caused by the Club or Club Personnel.

The Club’s obligations will not apply to the extent a claim is finally determined to have been directly caused by The Company’s fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence.

Subject to the same exclusions, the Club's indemnity above also covers third-party claims arising from the Club's or Club Personnel's misuse of Internal or VIP access, unauthorized communications, or unlawful collection, disclosure, retention, or use of personal information.

The Company Indemnification.

The Company will defend and indemnify the Club and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, contractors, temporary employees, and agents—collectively, the “Club Indemnified Parties”—from third-party claims alleging that the authorized use of the unmodified The Company technology directly infringes a United States patent, copyright, trademark, or trade-secret right.

The Company will have no obligation for claims arising from modifications not made or authorized by The Company; combinations with third-party products or services; unauthorized or unlawful use; continued use after The Company directs that use to stop; failure to install an available correction; or content, data, branding, instructions, or materials supplied by the Club, Club Personnel, or another third party.

Confidentiality and Nondisclosure Obligation.

The club may use The Company data only to operate authorized club features. It may not build customer lists from anonymous signals, export dancer or customer data, sell data, scrape, reidentify, or use commission or engagement information for discriminatory or retaliatory purposes. Confidential information includes nonpublic security information, NFC credentials, fee terms where designated, nonpublic user data, and incident information.

Permitted customer-list access is limited to information a customer expressly chooses to share with this Club and information submitted for a specific visit or request. Following alone does not authorize disclosure of contact details. Follower sharing, guest-list registration, pickup requests, and VIP participation do not constitute marketing consent. The Club may use each category only for its disclosed purpose and must obtain separate permission for marketing, including any consent required by applicable email, telephone, and text-message laws; it must honor opt-outs.

The Club must lawfully obtain invitation email addresses and permission to send VIP invitations, restrict customer information and VIP nicknames to authorized personnel, maintain reasonable safeguards, and promptly notify the Company of suspected unauthorized access or disclosure. It must not sell, export, republish, or reuse these records for unrelated purposes. The Club must honor notified sharing withdrawals and applicable access, correction, and deletion requests, deleting information no longer needed except for lawful retention. The Club is independently responsible for its use of received information; the Company remains responsible for its own legal duties. These requirements do not expand the existing data-export prohibition.

The Club will not at any time, or in any manner, whether during or after the termination of this Agreement, for any reason whatsoever (other than with the Company’s permission to promote and advance the business of the Company), reveal to any person or entity (both commercial and non-commercial) any of the trade secrets, proprietary, technical and/or confidential business information concerning the Company or third parties entrusting their own confidential information with the Company including, but not limited to: its marketing plans, proposals and strategies, customer and supplier lists and accounts, employees; pricing and costing policies, sales; research and development activities, product designs, prototypes and technical specifications; inventions (whether patentable or not), show-how and know-how; nonpublic financial information of the Company; or information received by the Company from others under an obligation of confidentiality, except as may be required in the ordinary course of performing his duties hereunder, without the express written permission of the Company. This restriction shall not apply to: (i) information that is disclosed generally or is in the public domain through no fault of the Club; (ii) information approved for release by written authorization of the Company; (iii) information that may be required by law or an order of any court, agency or proceeding to be disclosed; or (iv) information that Club can show was independently developed without reference to the Company’s confidential information.

Waiver.

Any waiver by the Company of a breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not operate or be construed as a waiver of any subsequent breach hereof.

Severability.

If one or more of the provisions contained in this Agreement shall for any reason be held to be excessively broad as to scope, activity or subject matter so as to be unenforceable at law, such provision(s) shall be construed and reformed by the appropriate judicial body by limiting and reducing it (or them), so as to be enforceable to the maximum extent compatible with the applicable law as it shall then appear.

Survival.

The obligations of the Club under this Agreement shall survive the termination of the Club’s relationship with the Company regardless of the manner of such termination.

Assignment.

The Company shall have the right to assign this Agreement to its successors and assigns and all covenants and agreements hereunder shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by the successors of the Company. The Club may not assign this Agreement.

Entire Agreement; Modifications.

This Agreement represents the entire agreement of the parties. Any modification of this Agreement must be in writing and signed by both parties.

Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Reasonableness of Terms.

This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of California without regards to its conflict of laws provisions. The parties agree to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in Los Angeles County, California, subject to the arbitration provision below. The Club recognizes and agrees that the enforcement of this Agreement is necessary to ensure the preservation, protection and continuity of the confidential business information, trade secrets and goodwill of the Company.

Construction.

The section headings contained in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not affect in any way the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. As used in this Agreement, the term “including” is illustrative and not limitative. As used herein the masculine form shall refer to the feminine where necessary, and vice-versa.

Arbitration.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, this Agreement as well as any claim, cause of action, or dispute that may arise between the Parties, are governed by the laws of the State of California without regard to conflict of law provisions. For claims permitted in court under the following paragraph, the Parties agree to submit and consent to the exclusive personal jurisdiction in, and the exclusive venue of the state and federal courts in Los Angeles County, California. The Parties hereby waive any right to seek another venue because of improper or inconvenient forum.

(a) Notwithstanding the foregoing, any controversies, disputes, actions, causes of action or other claims between the Parties arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination or validity hereof (a “Controversy”), shall be settled by arbitration administered by JAMS pursuant to its Comprehensive Arbitration Rules & Procedures (modified only as herein expressly provided), and judgment on any award rendered by the arbitrator may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. The arbitration shall be carried out in Los Angeles County, California, or by video conference before one arbitrator. The arbitrator may issue a default against any party that fails to participate in the arbitration. California substantive law applies; the Federal Arbitration Act governs the arbitration provision. The decision of the arbitrator on the points in dispute with respect to such Controversy will be final, non-appealable and binding and judgment on the award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. The parties agree that this clause has been included to rapidly and inexpensively resolve any Controversy, and that this clause shall be grounds for dismissal of any court action commenced by any party arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the breach, termination or validity hereof; provided that nothing in this subsection not this Agreement shall limit any party’s right to bring (i) post-arbitration actions seeking to enforce an arbitration award or (ii) actions seeking injunctive or other similar relief in the event of the breach or threatened breach of any of the provisions of this Agreement. The language used in the arbitration proceedings will be English.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, undersigned Club and the Company have executed this Agreement as of the date set forth above.
